title: Generate a report only when first requested
description: ReportGenerator wraps a costly computation (tracked via a call counter). getReport() should compute the report on the first call and cache the result — subsequent calls must return the same object without recomputing. The skeleton is in place; fill in the lazy init logic.
hints: Keep a private field for the cached report, initially null
In getReport(), check if the cache is null before calling compute()
compute() increments a counter — call it exactly once per ReportGenerator instance
issues: Calling compute() on every getReport() invocation wastes resources when the result never changes
There is no way to defer the cost until the report is actually needed
overallGoal: Use Lazy Initialization so the expensive computation runs exactly once per ReportGenerator instance, on the first call to getReport(), and is cached for all subsequent calls.
goals: getReport() returns the correct report content
compute() is called exactly once no matter how many times getReport() is invoked
Two separate ReportGenerator instances each perform their own independent lazy init
